one_line_contribution: A controlled dissociation claiming that what transfers across domains in GEPA-style reflective prompt optimization is a harvested, domain-scrubbed SYMPTOM/EDIT rulebook injected into the reflection step — not the optimized prompt skeleton — reported as a matched-budget sample-efficiency Pareto curve with a measured crossover budget rather than a leaderboard win.
closest_prior_work: The proposal positions itself against GEPA/MIPROv2/PromptBreeder/REMO/SPoT, but the family that actually threatens it is cross-run experience reuse for LLM systems, which is not cited at all: ExpeL (Zhao et al., AAAI 2024) already extracts natural-language insights from training-task trajectories into a retrieved insight pool and reports transfer to unseen tasks; AutoGuide (NeurIPS 2024) already induces state-conditioned 'situation -> guideline' rules from offline experience and retrieves them by match — structurally identical to SYMPTOM/EDIT retrieval by embedding similarity; Dynamic Cheatsheet (Suzgun et al., 2025) is a test-time memory of reusable strategies carried across tasks; and ACE / agentic context-engineering work (2025) literally builds and incrementally curates an evolving 'playbook' of bullets from execution feedback with a reflector/curator split. Against these, 'harvest failure->edit rules, scrub, retrieve, inject into the reflector' is not a new mechanism. REMO, which the proposal does cite, is dismissed for being single-benchmark and making no transfer claim — that is an evaluation delta, and the brief explicitly warns that a domain/eval swap scored as a modest delta rather than a contribution. What is genuinely new here is narrower than the title: the head-to-head artifact-vs-search-knowledge dissociation under a shared noise floor and matched token budget. That is a well-designed measurement of someone else's mechanism, not a new one.
strongest_objection: The central dissociation is guaranteed by the analysis plan rather than tested by it. The Falsifiable Predictions section asserts (a) prompt-skeleton warm start 'loses 2-5 points on distant pairs' and (b) playbook transfer 'is never worse than cold-start by more than the noise floor on any target'. Claim (b) is a null, and the Measurement section pre-declares an MDE of 1.5 points at n=30 plus a rule that 'effects below the null-replicate floor will be reported as null regardless of p-value'. So the playbook arm cannot be found to hurt unless it hurts by more than the design's own detection threshold, while the skeleton arm is predicted to hurt by an amount comfortably above it. Two separate one-sided conclusions at asymmetric power are not a dissociation; the paper needs the arm x source-target-distance interaction, powered for the interaction, and an equivalence test with a stated margin for 'never worse'. Three further defects compound this. (i) Experiment 6, the negative-transfer probe, transfers from a single distant source (symbolic BBH only) for both arms, but the headline playbook arm is built from six sources — so the probe's playbook has far fewer rules and different composition than the arm whose safety is being claimed, and 'which source' is confounded with 'how many rules'; the ablation 'playbook from one source domain vs six' concedes this axis matters. (ii) The shuffled-playbook control retrieves rules by anti-matching symptoms at identical token count. Anti-matched advice is plausibly worse than no advice (it misdirects the reflector), so this control can sit below cold-start and inflate the content-vs-conditioning contrast; the correct control is randomly-matched rules from the same pool. (iii) The crossover-budget promise — 'a bootstrap CI narrower than the checkpoint spacing' — is not supportable from the stated variance. Checkpoints are 25/50/100/200/300 and the crossover is predicted at 120-250, i.e. inside a single 100-rollout gap where the identification is pure interpolation, and a crossover is the ratio of a shrinking difference to a shrinking slope, whose bootstrap distribution with per-run SD ~3 and 30 paired observations will be wide or unbounded. Finally, the scrubbing loop is in tension with the paper's own value proposition: rules that fail the 6-way source-identification test are 're-scrubbed or dropped', which systematically selects the playbook toward generic, domain-free advice — precisely the direction that makes baseline (iv), the hand-written checklist, match it, which the proposal itself designates as the refutation condition.
what_would_fix_it: 1) Restate the headline as a pre-registered interaction: fit arm (playbook / skeleton) x distance (near / far) with task random effects, power the interaction rather than the two simple effects, and replace 'never worse than cold-start' with a TOST equivalence test against a stated margin. 2) Match the negative-transfer probe to the headline condition — run both a six-source and a one-source playbook against the six-source and one-source skeletons, so composition is not confounded with source distance. 3) Swap the anti-matched shuffle for randomly-matched rules from the same pool, and add an LLM-authored, unharvested rulebook matched in count, length, and format (see missing baseline). 4) Fix the budget arithmetic: cut arms (drop the SPoT-style soft-prompt reference and MIPROv2, which the brief already scopes out as a baseline-not-method) and spend the savings on seeds and on intermediate checkpoints at 75/150 so the crossover is bracketed rather than interpolated; report the crossover only when adjacent-checkpoint CIs actually separate, and otherwise report AUBC alone. 5) Report the leakage-test attrition rate and the pre/post-scrub playbooks as separate arms — if aggressive scrubbing is what makes rules safe, the harvesting claim is weaker than the framing. 6) Add an explicit preprint search over the experience-reuse/agent-memory family and state, rule by rule, what the harvested playbook contains that ExpeL-style insight pools and playbook-curation methods do not.
missing_baseline: An unharvested but format-matched rulebook: ask the same frontier reflection model to write 20-60 domain-general SYMPTOM/EDIT rules of <=60 tokens each, with no source runs, no traces, and no validated deltas, then retrieve and inject them by the identical top-3 embedding procedure. Baseline (iv) — a hand-written 'good prompting practices' checklist — is not this: it is human-authored, unmatched in count, length, and retrieval mechanism, and injected statically, so a win over it confounds 'harvesting from real runs' with 'having a retrieved, structured rulebook at all'. Since the entire cost and the entire claim of the paper is the harvesting (steps 2-3), the arm that isolates it is mandatory, not optional. Secondary omissions a reviewer will also raise: (a) a demonstration-only small-budget arm (bootstrapped few-shot selection, stopped at 25-50 rollouts), which is the strongest practical competitor exactly in the regime where the Pareto claim lives and which MIPROv2-at-full-budget does not stand in for; (b) an ExpeL / Dynamic-Cheatsheet-style memory baseline, i.e. the competing method family rather than a straw control; (c) a zero-rollout arm (playbook applied once to the seed prompt, no search), which bounds how much of the 50-rollout gain is search at all.
preprint_collision: The Preprint Collision Check field is empty, and nothing elsewhere in the submission substitutes for it: the Related Work section names indexed or well-known systems (GEPA, MIPROv2, PromptBreeder, SPoT/ATTEMPT, APE) plus two citations given without venue and unverifiable as written ('REMO, Wu & Qu, 2025' and 'PromptBridge / Oved et al., 2026'), and reports no searches, no date window, and no search terms. That is an unsearched claim of novelty and I score it as a weakness, not a neutral — especially given that the proposal's own citation list already reaches into 2026, i.e. exactly the fast-moving preprint layer it did not systematically check. Concretely, the search that was not run would have surfaced the collision: ExpeL (cross-task natural-language insight extraction and retrieval, with transfer experiments), AutoGuide (automatically induced context-conditioned guidelines selected by situation match), Dynamic Cheatsheet (persistent cross-task strategy memory at test time), Agent Workflow Memory (induced reusable routines carried to new tasks), and the 2025 agentic-context-engineering line that builds and curates an evolving 'playbook' of feedback-derived bullets with a reflector/curator split — the last of which uses the proposal's own central noun for the same object. I cannot certify that any single one of these already states this exact Pareto/dissociation claim on GEPA at matched rollout budgets, and I do not believe one does; the mechanism, however, is clearly not new, and the burden of showing otherwise was the proposal's and was not discharged. Until the authors run and report that search, the novelty score has to be set by the mechanism rather than by the framing.
